requirements.requirement: Local logs persist across node1 restarts and logging recovers afterward.
requirements.summary: A pre-restart marker was durably recorded with journald healthy, the reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and node1 returned running with journald active. The pre-restart marker remained readable, a new marker was recorded, both boots were listed, and journal integrity passed. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently confirm the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Local logs have a 14-day retention policy.
requirements.summary: The journald drop-in sets MaxRetentionSec=14day, the corresponding vacuum was applied, and the effective configuration still reported the 14-day policy after restart.

requirements.requirement: Local logging has bounded disk growth.
requirements.summary: The effective persistent policy limits journal use to 512M, preserves 1G of free space, and limits individual files to 64M. After restart, journald directly reported a 512M system-journal maximum while current usage was 10.6M.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Persistent journald storage survived an observed reboot, the effective 14-day retention policy remained active afterward, and journald recognized and enforced a 512M runtime maximum. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: The evidence does not span a full 14-day aging interval or fill the journal to its 512M limit; long-horizon expiration and pressure-driven pruning therefore rely on the directly observed effective journald policy and runtime-reported maximum rather than a prolonged stress test.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the drop-in and persistent journal directory established the requested policy; restarting, flushing, rotating, and vacuuming applied it; marker writes collected bounded persistence evidence; and the scheduled reboot fulfilled both the task's restart behavior test and the provider restart protocol. Post-executor observations show no failed services, unchanged listening endpoints aside from expected process-ID changes, healthy package state, and only normal reboot-regenerated systemd private directories. The restart protocol is complete and agrees with the fixed boot-identity observations.
